en: It's too late for that. The festival will run for a week, but that's not enough time. If you want to do it, it'll have to be next year.
Next year, huh? I don't know how things are gonna look that far ahead.
You won't be coming back next year?
I can't make any promises either way right now. Sorry.
No, it's all right! I might not even be working as a hostess anymore come next year.
Well if I do come back next year, I'm gonna make a big ass snow sculpture. Come and see it then.
All right! I'm looking forward to it!
Oh, the breeze feels so nice!
There's a definite scent of the sea in the air. It must be because we're so close to the ocean.
Yeah. Though speakin' on behalf of us girls, it's not always that great to be caught up in the sea breeze.
It's murder on your hair, and it can be mighty rough on the skin, too. It's a good idea to wear a hat if y'can.
I see. Maybe it's better to not walk around outside so much.
Nah, it's all right! It's fine so long as it's just a little bit.
Plus, I like how the ocean breeze smells. I think the scent of the salty air at sunset is wicked romantic.
I like it, too. Maybe being close to the ocean is one of the reasons why I chose to live here.
Oh yeah? Why's that?
Well, I used to live in Okinawa. Smelling the ocean air makes me kind of nostalgic.
Ah, I see. I guess bein' close to the sea is a big deciding factor for where y'choose to live, Kiryu-san.
Guess so. I hadn't really thought about it before now. Maybe I miss my old house.
Are y'feeling homesick?
Is that bad?
Oh no, not at all!
Perfect for a date. Back in Tokyo, you'd have to go all the way out to Odaiba to have a date like this.
It's not that great, really. There's a ton of food stalls, not to mention a buncha folks stumblin' around drunk, too.
Looking at the scenery's all well and good, but the romantic atmosphere is ruined by all the hustle and bustle around ya.
Heh. Well, that's life in the big city. It's better than some desolate harbor town.
Yeah, I guess. I suppose if y'were someplace way quiet, it'd feel like there's something missin'.
Maybe so.
Do you have a scent fetish?
What? Nah, not even! I'm sure there are smells that y'like too, Kiryu-san.
Sure, but I've never really considered any particular smells romantic.
It ain't just the smell! The fadin' light adds to the seaside atmosphere, too.
It sorta feels like Venice in Italy, or a port town ya'd see in a movie.
Have you ever been to Italy?
Well, no! But I know what it'd feel like!
Okay, if you say so.
I've been visiting Osaka for work for some time now, but I'm still not used to the city.
Really now?
Yeah. I'll crash at my office overnight, and when I stumble outside half-asleep in the morning, the signage wakes me right up.
Haha! Ain't nothin' wrong with that. Around my house there's nothin' but other houses. It's super borin'.
I stay overnight at my office in Tokyo often, so I've really never had an opportunity to live in a quiet residential neighborhood.
That ain't good. No matter how busy ya are, if ya don't try to get back home, you're just gonna wind up becomin' a workaholic.
You're absolutely right. I know it's not a good habit, but I haven't really developed an attachment to a home.
Why not? I figure a guy like you should be able to drop the cash to buy a house or two.
Actually, I was homeless at one point in my life.
Yeah, so I know that you don't need a home to live. There are more important things in life.
Whoa, that's some deep stuff! Maybe my own perspective on life would change if I gave livin' like that a shot.
Without a doubt. I wouldn't recommend it for a girl though.
Making time to go home is hard. Rent in Tokyo is high, so you have to live on the outskirts, and the commuting time borders on ridiculous.
There ya go again, sayin' that sorta thing. If you can spend all this money playin' around, why can't ya use it on rent?
I bet a guy like you could afford a place right smack-dab in the middle of Kamurocho.
You know, I was considering buying a place in Kamurocho Hills when units went on sale there.
For real? How come ya didn't buy it?
I mean, it was close to the office I have now, and if I bought a home there, it wouldn't be that much different than crashing at the office.
What're ya talkin' about!? If ya lived closer, you'd be able to get back home every day! Ya gotta have a proper work-life balance!
Hm. You make a good point.
I'm different. I'm no workaholic. My personal and work lives are so mixed up that I rarely focus one hundred percent on work.
I don't think ya should be boastin' about that.
Heh, guess not.
Only single guys can pull that off. If you were married, ya'd hafta go home and eat yer wife's cookin' every day, or it's divorce city for you.
Huh? It's not like you can't go out and eat. Business people have to network and socialize.
Nope! Eatin' out costs money. Ya gotta think about yer food expenses and eat dinner at home with your wife for maximum happiness!
Wow. You get so conscientious when money's involved.
We must be the only two here who came to Sotenbori on a date.
I don't think so. I've seen plenty of couples since we showed up.
But ain't they just tourists? Or maybe clients out with a hostess? This ain't a place folks usually come to on a date.
As a tourist spot, it's the heart of Osaka, but other than bein' a place to eat till ya drop, ain't much else goin' on here.
There are more fashionable places for shoppin', and if you're gonna go out to an arcade or karaoke, there are other places for that, too.
I see. So locals don't come here much. I haven't been here very long, so it hasn't lost its charm for me. But I guess it's different for you.
It ain't like that. I like this neighborhood, and there's nowhere better if ya wanna find a ton of tasty stuff to eat!
I definitely agree with you there.
Plus with school and work, I don't wanna go too much outta the way. Sotenbori is perfect.
I'm relieved to hear that. I don't know a thing about anywhere outside of Sotenbori, so I would have no idea where to take you out to eat.
Ya don't gotta worry there! I'm the one leadin' ya around today. You just relax and enjoy Osaka, Akiyama-san!
That sounds good to me.
Want to go somewhere else? We are on a date, so I'm okay going someplace more romantic.
Where do ya wanna go?

en: To be honest, I don't really know Osaka all that well.
I figured as much. That's why I went and suggested we do Sotenbori.
A visitor like yerself should be a visitor and let a local show ya around.
Thanks, I really appreciate it.
I don't care so long as I'm with you.
What!? Where'd that come from all a sudden!?
I have fun just by being with you. I don't care where we go, even if it's not some popular date spot.
I'd actually prefer going to some little hole-in-the-wall with you, just the two of us.
Hey, knock it off. You're makin' me blush.
I always see you in noisy places like this, so I'm curious to see what you're like when you're in a different environment.
Aww, I'm the same no matter where I go.
If ya keep sayin' weird stuff, I might start gettin' mad at ya. Hehe.
It's a nice change of pace to stroll through town like this. I typically drive to the places I want to go.
Yeah, I get what you mean.
I mean, not that I drive a car or anything. I'm usually just running around trying to meet deadlines.
Hehe! So, you don't get the opportunity to slow down and take in the sights much, either?
Nope. Plus, there's nothing but buildings in this part of town. The greenery of the park is kind of relaxing.
We have a small garden at our home. The flowers aren't in bloom right now, unfortunately, but come spring it's quite lovely.
I'd love to see it! Single-family homes with their own gardens must be nice.
I'll have to show you pictures sometime. I take plenty of photos every year, so you can see the garden in all four seasons!
Hey, that sounds nice! I'd like to see it firsthand, too.
Oh my, you want to come to my house?
It really won't be worth your while to visit right now, though. You'll have to wait until spring.
Oh, no big deal. Haha. It was a stupid thing for me to say anyway.
I'll be sure to bring some pictures for you to see instead. I do hope you'll like them!
It ain't really the garden I'm interested in.
Isn't it a pain to maintain? I'm guessing weeds grow if you're not careful, and I bet it's hard to find the time to take care of it.
That's true. My father used to take care of the garden on his days off, but we now have to hire help to do it.
Yikes! Bet that's expensive.
It is. That's why I've recently taken to only growing flowers I'm able to care for on my own.
Seems like kind of a waste to only use a garden for that. There must be something you can do to grow more.
Perhaps so. Hmm.
Maybe I should fill the rest with artificial flowers? At least they wouldn't attract insects.
That's no good. A garden is supposed to be about the beauty of nature. What's the point if the nature is fake?
Very true. I'll discuss it with my mother.
I've got an amazing garden, too!
Oh? You live in your own house as well, Shinada-san?
Well, no. I live on my building's rooftop. Let's call it the penthouse.
All I have to do is step outside and I've got a view of all Kineicho. It's not a literal garden, but it feels like one when I'm staring out at it.
Oh my, that sounds lovely! I've lived in a house my entire life, so that kind of scenery strikes me as quite dreamy!
If I ever have the opportunity to move, perhaps I'll move into a condominium!
I think you'd really like it!
Though I wouldn't recommend living in a place like mine.
Oh, that's right. The other day I was walking around here and had a bit of trouble.
Whoa, really? What happened?
I came across an older woman who was lost, and so, naturally, I approached her and offered to help her find her way.
But it turned out I didn't know how to get to where she was headed, and so in the end I wasn't able to give her the directions she needed.
Huh? Aren't you from here though, Shion-chan? Do you not know this neighborhood?
I don't, no. And it's not as if I'm from another place like you, Shinada-san. I'm a local, so it's embarrassing to not know these things.
You're so kind! Heck, if I ran into that sort of situation, I'd probably forget all about it right afterwards.
It's because I don't get to see my maternal grandmother since she's in France, and my father's mother died when I was young. I try to help the elderly where I can.
But in this situation, I was completely useless. I just wound up making things worse for her.
I think it's nice of you to feel that way. I'm sure this woman was happy that you at least tried to help her out.
Yeah! So if you ever run into that sorta thing again, don't doubt yourself. Try and offer whatever help you can!
If you say so, Shinada-san!
In that case, I should walk around this neighborhood more often. That way I can familiarize myself with these streets and provide directions to someone else in the future.
Sure! And I can go with you!
Hey, it happens. These days, I don't think even locals know their town from top to bottom like that.
Most people are probably unfamiliar with places right in their neighborhood, if they usually don't have any business going there.
I certainly agree, but that's no excuse to remain in a state of willful ignorance, don't you think?
In a perfect world, sure, but I don't think it's realistic to know the whole city. I imagine even the police don't know it inside-out.
But shouldn't we try to help for that very reason? Even if you take someone to a police box, there are probably places a policeman wouldn't know.
Yeah, the cops aren't going to help a guy who's looking for some sex club, that's for sure. That's when you go find an info booth.
That's why I think I should try my best to help people. We should all help one another.
I get you. A town is only as good as the people who've come together to live there.
You should explore more. You can never know too much about the place you live.
But how would I go about becoming more knowledgeable about this town?
Well, looking at a map is one thing, but as they say, seeing is believing. You have to check places out in person.
You can try to make a point of checking out a new place each week. You should become pretty familiar with the town within a year, I'd say.
